title: ReviewDecision
description: Evidence-linked, bounded-authority review verdict emitted by a Reviewer (judicial gate, non-mutating). Domain-general: applies to code, answers, plans, summaries, math. The hard-stop channel (`blocking.tripwire` + `blocking.blocking_issues`) is STRUCTURALLY SEPARATE from the advisory channel (`advisory.score` / `non_blocking_issues` / `feedback`) so a consumer computing 'must this hard-stop?' reads ONLY `blocking` and never lets an advisory score bleed into a blocking verdict (safety_gate.py / Agents-SDK guardrail semantics). Immutable once emitted; version/append rather than mutate.

schema_version.description: Artifact schema version (semver). Optional on emission — the trace-store emission layer (RA-10) stamps it; reviewers need not produce it.

decision_id.description: Unique identifier for this decision (UUID recommended).

candidate_ref.description: Reference (package_id) of the CandidatePackage under review.

rubric_ref.description: Reference (rubric_id@version) of the ReviewRubric applied, if any.

subtask_id.description: Subtask/step this verdict covers (compat with ArchitectReview.subtask_id).

reviewed_at.description: ISO 8601 timestamp when the verdict was produced.

decision.description: Bounded-authority verdict. reject_to_empty = a bad plan/output is worse than none, discard rather than iterate. request_evidence = verdict withheld pending verifier_requests. abstain (v1.1, spec §9.2) = the package is insufficient AND no permitted evidence request can resolve it — the reviewer declines to decide (distinct from escalate). escalate = defer to a higher tier / human for a policy-defined case.

confidence.description: Reviewer's calibrated confidence in the VERDICT itself (how sure am I this decision is correct), distinct from advisory.score (how good the candidate is). Used by the FA/FR calibration ledger.

human_review_required.description: Reviewer requests human adjudication before the decision is enforced.

blocking.description: Hard-stop channel. Orthogonal to the advisory channel; only these fields may gate a bounce-to-author / reject.

tripwire.description: True = a hard invariant was violated; the candidate MUST NOT pass regardless of advisory score.

blocking_issues.description: Issues that individually justify a hard stop.

advisory.description: Advisory channel. Informational only — MUST NOT be used to compute a hard-stop.

score.description: Advisory quality score of the candidate in [0,1].

non_blocking_issues.description: Issues worth surfacing that do not by themselves block.

feedback.description: Free-form advisory feedback routed to the author on request_changes.

telemetry.description: v1.1 (spec §5.4 raw-confidence invariant / §6.4 / §11.1). TELEMETRY ONLY. Nothing in this block may independently trigger approval, blocking, or escalation — enforcement authority derives from empirically calibrated cohort risk (see DecisionEnvelope.calibration + AssuranceProfile), never from what the model says about itself. Recorded for calibration/monitoring; the deterministic policy reducer MUST ignore it as an enforcement signal.

raw_model_confidence.description: The reviewer model's self-reported (verbalized) confidence. TELEMETRY-ONLY — distinct from the top-level `confidence` (verdict-calibration input) and from calibrated cohort risk. Models are systematically overconfident (R8/R9); this number never gates.

evidence.description: Links grounding the verdict. Domain-general evidence kinds (answer spans and scorer/retrieval results, not only file_span/test_result).

verifier_requests.description: Objective checks the reviewer wants run (the request_evidence payload). Consumed by the verifier-request adapter; results return as a VerificationReport.

provenance.description: Who/what produced this verdict (reviewer model, quant, flag state).

location.description: Domain-general locator: 'path:line', answer char span, retrieval doc id, etc.

evidence_ref.description: Points into evidence[] (by index or ref) grounding this issue.

criterion_id.description: v1.1 (spec §5.2/§6.4/§9.2). Criterion this finding is scoped to (keys into the AssuranceProfile.criteria / verifier_registry). A blocking finding SHOULD map to exactly one criterion; the reducer's `has_grounded_blocking_finding()` reads this + `evidence_ref`/`unsupported`.

remediation_target.description: v1.1 (spec §6.4). Who owns the repair: 'architect' | 'worker' | 'author' | role id. The reviewer never mutates the authoritative artifact (§5.1); repair routes here.

unsupported.description: v1.1 (spec §9.2). True = this finding carries NO evidence reference (the reviewer is asserting it without grounding). An unsupported blocking finding cannot ground a calibrated rejection in the reducer (§8 step 5).

ref.description: Pointer/URI/id to the evidence source (path, test id, gate id, trace event id, protocol-id).

weight.description: Relative importance of this evidence to the verdict.

verifier.description: Verifier identifier (gate name, scorer id, checker name).

target.description: Artifact/output ref the verifier should run against.
